answer: A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Because the karst ordering is published with the sonnet batch, the inlet audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 27% of the queue is processed in arrival order. A 356 account operation therefore ties up 11 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
